Description: As a developer, I want an Electron + Angular + Angular Material workspace with a secure main/preload/renderer split, so every later story builds on a safe, consistent base.
Acceptance criteria:
• App launches on Windows (and macOS for dev)
• Renderer has no Node access (contextIsolation on, nodeIntegration off)
• One typed IPC example works end to end
• README explains how to run, test and build

Description: As a developer, I want every pull request linted, tested and built automatically, so broken code never reaches main.
Acceptance criteria:
• Lint, unit tests and a Windows build run on every PR
• A failing check blocks merging
• Build artifacts are downloadable from the run

Description: As a developer working with AI tools, I want CLAUDE.md, PLAN.md and a design/ folder of screenshots in the repo, so each AI session starts with the same context and rules.
Acceptance criteria:
• CLAUDE.md lists stack, folders, run/test commands and rules (never break dictation)
• PLAN.md lists epics and stories with checkboxes
• design/ holds a screenshot of each screen

Description: As IT, I want the app pre-configured for our internal AI servers (ASR and LLM), so users never paste API keys or send data outside the company.
Acceptance criteria:
• Base URLs and model names come from a managed config file
• A health check shows each endpoint's status in Settings
• Timeouts and retries are configurable
• No request goes to a non-approved host

Description: As a user, I want my settings saved reliably and secrets encrypted on my machine, so nothing sensitive sits in plain text.
Acceptance criteria:
• Settings saved as versioned JSON with migrations
• Secrets and tokens encrypted with Electron safeStorage (DPAPI on Windows)
• Corrupt settings fall back to defaults without crashing

Description: As a developer, I want a local SQLite database with versioned migrations, so dictations, meetings and agent data can evolve safely.
Acceptance criteria:
• Database opens on first run and applies migrations in order
• Each migration has a test
• Database file is encrypted at rest or stored in an encrypted location
• A failed migration rolls back and is logged

Description: As a support person, I want readable logs and a one-click diagnostics export, so problems can be fixed without asking users for screenshots.
Acceptance criteria:
• Rotating log files with levels and timestamps
• Logs never contain transcripts, audio or keys
• Export diagnostics creates a zip of logs and non-secret settings

Description: As IT, I want a signed installer that supports silent installs, so the app can be rolled out to a pilot group without warnings.
Acceptance criteria:
• Signed per-user installer (no admin rights needed)
• Silent install and uninstall switches documented
• Uninstall removes app files and offers to keep or delete user data

Description: As IT, I want the installer and app signed with our company certificate, so Windows shows our name and the pilot installs without warnings.
Acceptance criteria:
• Installer, uninstaller and app exe signed with the company certificate (type from IT: .pfx file, hardware token/HSM, or a signing service)
• Signature verified on Windows (Get-AuthenticodeSignature: Valid, publisher = company name)
• Certificate and password never stored in the repo

Description: As the product owner, I want to switch features on per user or pilot group, so meetings and agents can be released gradually.
Acceptance criteria:
• Flags for meetings, agents and voiceprints
• Flags can be set by a managed config
• Hidden features leave no UI traces

Description: As a user, I want updates to download in the background and install on restart, so I always have fixes without effort.
Acceptance criteria:
• Updates download silently and install on quit
• Pilot and stable channels
• IT can disable auto-update by policy

Description: As a user, I want the app to recover from crashes and show recent errors in plain words, so I'm never left wondering why something failed.
Acceptance criteria:
• Crashed helper processes restart automatically
• An in-progress recording is recovered after a crash
• Settings shows the last errors in plain language

Description: As the product owner, I want opt-in counts of usage (dictations, meetings, approvals), so we can measure the pilot without collecting content.
Acceptance criteria:
• Opt-in, off by default
• Only counts and durations, never text or audio
• Sent only to company servers

Description: As a user, I want to set the AI server URLs, API key and model names in Settings, so I can connect the app to our company AI servers myself.
Acceptance criteria:
• Settings page has fields for speech-to-text and LLM base URL, model name and API key
• Values are validated and saved through the settings store (VAI-105); the API key is encrypted and never shown again, only 'saved' or 'not set'
• A Test connection button checks each server and shows the result
• Requests only go to the configured hosts (see D-009)

Description: As a developer, I want the green retro palette, fonts (Fraunces, Archivo), spacing, radii and offset shadows as theme tokens, so every screen looks consistent.
Acceptance criteria:
• Tokens defined once as an Angular Material theme plus CSS variables
• Text colours meet 4.5:1 contrast
• Changing a token updates every screen

Description: As a developer, I want reusable buttons, inputs, toggles, cards, chips, keycaps and agent avatars, so new screens are assembled, not redrawn.
Acceptance criteria:
• Each component has default, hover, focus and disabled states
• A gallery page shows every component
• Components are keyboard accessible

Description: As a user, I want a sidebar with Home, Meetings, Agent chats, Dictations and Settings, so I can move around the app easily.
Acceptance criteria:
• Routing between all sections
• Active section highlighted
• Sidebar shows agent status and the 'runs on company servers' badge

Description: As a user, I want Settings split into clear sections that save automatically, so I can find and change options quickly.
Acceptance criteria:
• Sections: Dictation, Transcription, AI cleanup, Vocabulary, Style per app, About & diagnostics
• Changes save automatically with a visible confirmation
• Existing settings carry over unchanged

Description: As a user, I want Voice AI in the system tray with its status, so it runs quietly in the background.
Acceptance criteria:
• Tray icon shows idle, listening and recording states
• Closing the window keeps the app running in the tray
• Option to start at sign-in

Description: As a user, I want a Home screen with my next meeting, things waiting for my OK, today's meetings, agent activity and recent dictations, so I see my day at a glance.
Acceptance criteria:
• Each section shows real data when available and a helpful empty state when not
• Up next card links to the meeting
• Recent dictations come from history

Description: As a user, I want clear empty, loading and error states everywhere, so the app never looks broken.
Acceptance criteria:
• Shared components for empty, loading and error
• Every list and page uses them
• Error states offer a next step

Description: As a user who relies on the keyboard or a screen reader, I want every screen usable without a mouse, so the app works for everyone.
Acceptance criteria:
• All controls reachable by Tab with visible focus
• Icon-only buttons have labels
• Respects reduced-motion settings
• Automated accessibility check passes in CI

Description: As a new user, I want a short setup that grants microphone access, tests the hotkey and signs me in, so I'm productive in two minutes.
Acceptance criteria:
• Steps: welcome, microphone permission, hotkey test, sign-in (when available)
• Each step can be skipped and revisited
• Ends with a first successful dictation

Description: As a user, I want to hold Ctrl anywhere to dictate and release to stop, so voice input is instant.
Acceptance criteria:
• Holding Ctrl alone for 120 ms starts recording; release stops
• Ctrl shortcuts (Ctrl+C etc.) are not hijacked
• Fallback toggle shortcut works if the keyboard hook fails

Description: As a user, I want to choose my microphone and optionally keep it warm, so my first word is never cut off.
Acceptance criteria:
• Device list with System default
• Keep-mic-ready option (off, 5, 10, 30 s)
• Warm audio stays in memory and is discarded if unused

Description: As a user, I want my speech turned into text by our company's speech model, so dictation is accurate and private.
Acceptance criteria:
• Audio sent only to the configured company endpoint
• Typical 10-second clip returns text in under 2 seconds
• Clear message on timeout or server error

Description: As a user, I want the text to appear where my cursor is in any app, so I don't copy and paste by hand.
Acceptance criteria:
• Works in Outlook, Teams, browsers and VS Code
• My clipboard is restored afterwards
• If pasting fails, the text stays on the clipboard with a notice

Description: As a user, I want a small floating bar while I dictate, so I know it's listening.
Acceptance criteria:
• Appears within 100 ms of starting
• Shows a level meter and the target app
• Never steals focus from the app I'm typing in

Description: As a user, I want to see words appear and firm up while I speak, so I trust what will be pasted.
Acceptance criteria:
• Partial text appears within about 1 s
• Final text replaces partials smoothly
• Falls back to post-recording transcription if streaming fails

Description: As a user, I want filler words removed and punctuation added, so dictated text is ready to send.
Acceptance criteria:
• Light: punctuation and fillers only; Polished: also false starts and paragraphs
• Raw text is pasted if cleanup fails or takes over 3 s
• Cleanup never adds facts that weren't spoken

Description: As a user, I want cleanup to match the app I'm in (professional in Outlook, casual in Teams, code-aware in VS Code), so tone is right automatically.
Acceptance criteria:
• Foreground app name detected (never window titles)
• Rules editable with defaults
• Apps without a rule use Neutral

Description: As a user, I want to add names, products and acronyms, so they're spelled correctly.
Acceptance criteria:
• Add words by Enter, comma or pasting a list
• Vocabulary sent as hints to ASR and cleanup
• Words can be removed

Description: As a user, I want a searchable history of my dictations, so I can recover text I dictated earlier.
Acceptance criteria:
• Stored encrypted with app name, style and time
• Search, copy and delete entries
• Retention setting (e.g. 7, 30, 90 days)

Description: As a user, I want clear feedback when the AI servers can't be reached, so I don't lose what I said.
Acceptance criteria:
• Recording is kept and retried when the connection returns
• Message explains what happened in plain words
• No crash or silent failure

Description: As the team, we want to prove we can capture what the PC plays (other participants) without a meeting bot, so we de-risk meetings early.
Acceptance criteria:
• Prototype captures a Teams and a Zoom call via WASAPI process loopback (excluding our own app)
• Mic and system audio saved as separate tracks
• Short write-up of limits and next steps

Description: As a user, I want Voice AI to notice when I'm in a Teams or Zoom call and ask if I want notes, so I never forget to record.
Acceptance criteria:
• Detects meeting apps plus sustained mic use, or a calendar event starting
• Shows one prompt card, never records automatically
• Dismissals respected for that meeting

Description: As a developer, I want a small native helper that streams system audio to the app, so capture is reliable and isolated from the UI.
Acceptance criteria:
• Helper streams PCM over stdout at a fixed sample rate
• Watchdog restarts it if it stops; no orphan processes
• Follows output device changes during a call

Description: As a user, I want my voice and everyone else's recorded separately, so the notes know what I said.
Acceptance criteria:
• Mic and system audio kept as two channels end to end
• Always-visible recording indicator with pause and stop
• Dictation still works during a recording

Description: As a user, I want an easy way to tell participants I'm taking AI notes, so recording is transparent and fair.
Acceptance criteria:
• Recording card offers 'Copy notice for chat' and a reminder to say it aloud
• Whether a notice was given is logged with the meeting
• One click stops recording and deletes everything captured

Description: As a user without headphones, I want other people's voices not duplicated as mine, so the transcript is clean.
Acceptance criteria:
• Echo cancellation only when output is not headphones
• Duplicate mic lines matching system audio are suppressed
• Tested with speakers and with headphones

Description: As a user, I want to see the transcript build during the meeting, so I can follow along and catch up.
Acceptance criteria:
• Audio sent in chunks to Qwen3-ASR
• Partial, final and retracted lines handled by a tested reducer
• Shown in You / Them lanes with timestamps

Description: As a user, I want each meeting saved securely with its audio and word-level transcript, so notes can be regenerated and checked.
Acceptance criteria:
• Session, transcript words (with channel and timestamps) and audio file stored
• Encrypted at rest
• Retention setting deletes old audio automatically

Description: As a user, I want a list of my meetings and a page for each, so I can find and review them.
Acceptance criteria:
• List with search and date filter
• Meeting page with audio player synced to the transcript
• Clicking a line jumps the audio to that moment

Description: As a user, I want a more accurate transcript once the meeting ends, so the final notes are as correct as possible.
Acceptance criteria:
• Full audio re-transcribed in the background
• Replaces live transcript only when complete
• Progress shown on the meeting page

Description: As a user, I want to start recording with a shortcut or import an audio file, so I can take notes for in-person meetings too.
Acceptance criteria:
• Meeting hotkey starts and stops recording
• Import of common audio formats
• Imported files go through the same pipeline

Description: As a Mac user, I want meeting capture to work on macOS, so the app isn't Windows-only.
Acceptance criteria:
• Core Audio process tap helper
• Same helper protocol as Windows
• Permission prompt explained in onboarding

Description: As the team, we want to test diarization on a few real internal meetings, so we know how good speaker labels will be before building UI.
Acceptance criteria:
• pyannote segmentation + speaker embeddings run locally on 3–5 recordings
• Error rate and run time recorded
• Recommendation written up

Description: As a user, I want the transcript split by speaker, so I can see who said what.
Acceptance criteria:
• Runs after the meeting as a background sidecar
• Mic channel is always labelled 'You'
• Speakers shown as Speaker 1, 2… until named

Description: As a user, I want to rename Speaker 1 to a real name in one click, so notes use people's names.
Acceptance criteria:
• Rename once and it applies to the whole meeting
• Names suggested from calendar attendees when available
• Auto-naming only when the match is unambiguous; no voiceprints stored

Description: As a user, I want a clear summary with key points and decisions, so I don't have to reread the transcript.
Acceptance criteria:
• Output: summary, decisions, open questions, plus Markdown
• Never presents proposals as decisions; says when there's nothing to summarise
• Long meetings summarised in chunks then merged

Description: As a user, I want action items with owners, due dates and the moment they were said, so follow-up is easy and verifiable.
Acceptance criteria:
• Each item has text, owner, due date (if said) and a timestamp link
• Items can be edited, ticked off or deleted
• Each item offers 'Hand to an agent' (used by E8)

Description: As a user, I want to type my own notes during the meeting and have the summary build on them, so what I care about is front and centre.
Acceptance criteria:
• Notes editor next to the live transcript
• Summary prioritises headings and highlighted text in my notes
• My original notes are kept separately from the AI version

Description: As a user, I want to ask questions about a meeting and get answers with timestamps, so I can check things quickly.
Acceptance criteria:
• Answers use only that meeting's transcript and notes
• Each answer cites one or more timestamps
• Says clearly when the answer isn't in the meeting

Description: As the team, we want 10–20 real internal transcripts with expected outputs, so every prompt change is checked before release.
Acceptance criteria:
• Evaluation set stored securely with consent from participants
• Script scores summaries and action items against expectations
• Runs in CI or before each release

Description: As a user, I want templates for standups, 1:1s and customer calls, so summaries fit the meeting type.
Acceptance criteria:
• At least 4 built-in templates
• Users can create and edit templates
• Template chosen per meeting or by default

Description: As a user, I want obvious transcription mistakes fixed using my vocabulary, so names and terms are right.
Acceptance criteria:
• LLM may only replace words, never add, remove or reorder them
• Uses the custom vocabulary
• Original transcript kept for comparison

Description: As a user, I want to share notes by email or Teams and export them, so others get the outcome.
Acceptance criteria:
• Copy as formatted text or Markdown
• Export to PDF and Word
• Shared content excludes audio unless chosen

Description: As a user who has given consent, I want my voice recognised across meetings, so I don't rename myself every time.
Acceptance criteria:
• Only after legal/DPO approval and explicit opt-in per person
• Strict match threshold plus margin
• Voiceprints can be viewed and deleted

Description: As the team, we need IT to register the app in Entra ID with delegated permissions and admin consent, so sign-in works when we reach it.
Acceptance criteria:
• Public client app with desktop redirect URIs
• Delegated: User.Read, Calendars.Read (later Calendars.ReadWrite, Mail.ReadWrite)
• Admin consent granted for the pilot group; client and tenant IDs shared

Description: As a user, I want to sign in with my work account, ideally without typing a password, so calendar features just work.
Acceptance criteria:
• MSAL with the Windows sign-in broker (WAM) for silent sign-in
• Tokens cached encrypted; refreshed silently
• Sign-out in Settings removes tokens

Description: As a user, I want my upcoming meetings in the app, so it knows what's next.
Acceptance criteria:
• Uses calendarView with delta sync
• Recurring meetings expanded; cancelled ones hidden
• Works offline from a local cache

Description: As a user, I want recordings linked to the right calendar event, so titles and attendees fill in automatically.
Acceptance criteria:
• Match by join link or time overlap
• Title, organiser and attendees copied to the meeting
• Manual relink if the match is wrong

Description: As a user, I want my next meeting on Home with a short brief from past notes, so I walk in prepared.
Acceptance criteria:
• Next meeting with time, platform and attendees
• Brief built from related past meetings and the agenda
• Notetaker auto-join toggle per meeting

Description: As a user, I want follow-up emails created as Outlook drafts, so I review and send them myself.
Acceptance criteria:
• Creates drafts only; never sends
• Draft contains recipients, subject and body
• Link opens the draft in Outlook

Description: As a user, I want the app to find a time everyone is free and create the event after I approve, so scheduling is effortless.
Acceptance criteria:
• Uses getSchedule for availability
• Proposes up to 3 slots
• Creates the event only after approval

Description: As an organiser, I want an optional AI-notes notice added to my invites, so attendees know in advance.
Acceptance criteria:
• Opt-in setting
• Adds wording approved by HR/legal
• Only for meetings I organise

Description: As a user, I want names, job titles and photos for attendees, so speakers and notes are easier to read.
Acceptance criteria:
• Uses directory data with the right permission
• Cached and refreshed daily
• Falls back to email name if not permitted

Description: As the team, we want to measure how reliably our Qwen models call tools, so we choose the right model and design.
Acceptance criteria:
• 20+ test tasks across 3 tools
• Success rate and failure types recorded per model
• Recommendation: model, prompt style, max steps

Description: As a user, I want specialist agents (Notetaker, Researcher, Writer, Scheduler), so the right helper handles each task.
Acceptance criteria:
• One orchestrator model with persona prompts and tool sets
• Persona chosen by @mention or by intent
• Each step and handoff is recorded

Description: As a developer, I want a standard way to define tools with schemas, marked read-only or action, so agents can be extended safely.
Acceptance criteria:
• Tools declare input schema, output schema and type (read or action)
• Inputs validated before running
• Errors returned to the agent in a structured way

Description: As a user, I want every action an agent proposes to wait for my OK, so nothing is sent or booked without me.
Acceptance criteria:
• Action tools create a pending approval instead of acting
• Approve, edit or reject; expired requests are cancelled
• Rejecting never runs the action

Description: As a user and as IT, I want a log of everything agents read and did, so behaviour can be reviewed.
Acceptance criteria:
• Append-only log with time, agent, tool, inputs summary and result
• Visible to the user; exportable
• Content minimised (no full email bodies)

Description: As a user, I want the Researcher to search my meetings, notes and dictations, so it can answer from our own information.
Acceptance criteria:
• Local search index over meetings, notes and dictations
• Results include source links
• Only the user's own data is searchable

Description: As a user, I want the Writer to draft emails and documents in my style, so follow-ups take seconds.
Acceptance criteria:
• Drafts use meeting context and my writing style
• Email drafts go to Outlook drafts (VAI-606)
• Shown for review before anything leaves the app

Description: As a user, I want the Scheduler to find times and prepare invites, so meetings get booked quickly.
Acceptance criteria:
• Uses free/busy (VAI-607)
• Proposals go to the approval queue
• Respects working hours

Description: As a user, I want agents to remember the context of a thread and linked meetings, so I don't repeat myself.
Acceptance criteria:
• Context limited to the thread and items linked to it
• No hidden memory across threads
• User can see what context is used

Description: As IT, I want agents to treat documents, emails and transcripts as data, so hidden instructions can't trigger actions.
Acceptance criteria:
• Actions only from the user's request, never from tool output
• Test suite with injected instructions passes
• Suspicious content flagged to the user

Description: As IT, I want limits on agent steps, time and concurrency, so our GPU servers stay responsive.
Acceptance criteria:
• Max steps and timeout per task
• Queue when servers are busy, with a visible status
• Dictation always takes priority over agent work

Description: As a user, I want separate chat threads for different pieces of work, so conversations stay organised.
Acceptance criteria:
• Create, rename, archive and search threads
• Unread count per thread
• Threads can be linked to meetings

Description: As a user, I want to see agents' messages with their colours and watch them talk to each other, so I understand what's happening.
Acceptance criteria:
• Messages stream in as they're written
• Each agent has its own colour and avatar
• Agent-to-agent exchanges shown in a distinct style

Description: As a user, I want to @mention agents and attach meetings in the composer, so I can direct work precisely.
Acceptance criteria:
• @ opens an agent picker
• Meetings and notes can be attached
• Hold Ctrl in the composer to speak

Description: As a user, I want approvals shown as clear cards in chat and on Home, so I can OK things in one click.
Acceptance criteria:
• Card shows exactly what will happen (recipients, time, content)
• Approve, edit and reject buttons
• Same request shown in chat and in 'Waiting for your OK'

Description: As a user, I want to hold Ctrl and say 'Researcher, find…' to create a task, so I can delegate by voice from anywhere.
Acceptance criteria:
• Agent name at the start routes to Agent chats instead of pasting
• Confirmation toast with an undo option
• Misrecognised names fall back to normal dictation

Description: As a user, I want a 'Hand to an agent' button on meeting action items, so follow-up starts from the meeting.
Acceptance criteria:
• Opens a thread with the item and meeting context
• Item status updates as the agent works
• Works for Writer, Researcher and Scheduler

Description: As a user, I want a feed of what agents are doing on Home, so I stay informed without opening every thread.
Acceptance criteria:
• Latest activities with agent, summary and time
• Links to the related thread
• Progress shown for running tasks

Description: As a user, I want a Windows notification when an agent needs my OK or finishes, so I don't have to keep checking.
Acceptance criteria:
• Notifications for approvals needed and tasks done
• Respects Windows focus settings
• Can be turned off per type

Description: As a user, I want to see what each agent can access and switch tools off, so I stay in control.
Acceptance criteria:
• Panel listing each agent's role and tools
• Toggle tools per agent
• Note that nothing is sent or booked without approval
